(i) **Zener Diode Regulator Range Calculations:**
Given: $V_i = 50\text{ V}$, $R = 1\text{ k}\Omega$, $V_Z = 10\text{ V}$, $I_{ZM} = 32\text{ mA}$.
- **Minimum Load Resistance ($R_{L\text{min}}$) & Maximum Load Current ($I_{L\text{max}}$):**
  - Maximum current through series resistor $R$: $I_R = \frac{V_i - V_Z}{R} = \frac{50 - 10}{1\text{ k}\Omega} = 40\text{ mA}$.
  - For Zener to remain in breakdown, $I_Z > 0$. Let $I_{Z\text{min}} = 0$.
  - $I_{L\text{max}} = I_R - I_{Z\text{min}} = 40\text{ mA} - 0 = 40\text{ mA}$.
  - $R_{L\text{min}} = \frac{V_Z}{I_{L\text{max}}} = \frac{10\text{ V}}{40\text{ mA}} = 250\Omega$.

- **Maximum Load Resistance ($R_{L\text{max}}$) & Minimum Load Current ($I_{L\text{min}}$):**
  - For Zener to operate safely up to $I_{ZM} = 32\text{ mA}$:
  - $I_{L\text{min}} = I_R - I_{ZM} = 40\text{ mA} - 32\text{ mA} = 8\text{ mA}$.
  - $R_{L\text{max}} = \frac{V_Z}{I_{L\text{min}}} = \frac{10\text{ V}}{8\text{ mA}} = 1.25\text{ k}\Omega$.

- **Maximum Wattage Rating of Diode ($P_{ZM}$):**
  $$P_{ZM} = V_Z \times I_{ZM} = 10\text{ V} \times 32\text{ mA} = 320\text{ mW}$|

---(ii) **Circuit Design for Given Output:**
The output waveform shows a clamped/shifted sine wave: $V_o = V_m + V$ (positive clamper or biased positive peak detector). This requires a diode pointing upwards/downwards combined with a DC voltage source in series with the diode or capacitor to shift the waveform vertically by a DC level.
proTip: In Zener regulator design, always ensure that load resistance does not drop below $R_{L\text{min}}$, otherwise the Zener diode goes out of regulation.
